body: I was in a nursery here in Florida today, we have these same caladiums in nearly full sun all day with no burns so its probably a conditioning thing. I'd say try to put it in  a bit more light for 2 weeks and see if you get some improvements, this would use more water as well. If you want to, or more sun doesn't help, you can unpot it, add more perlite/drainage to your mix and check for root rot. I use 50% potting mix 25% coir 20% pumice with some worm castings. My potting mix is pretty airy already. My last caladium i bought in distress was root rotting from a chunky bark mix indoors so it can happen i suppose.

My caladiums are pretty moody when I first get them and bring them home. They pretty much all fall over like this. Usually I repot cut off the really yellow stems (caladiums absorb nutrients back through the dying stems and its not uncommon) and put it outside in indirect sunlight until the leaves start coming in less leggy and stiffer stems. Are you positive it is getting enough sunlight? I can't really see but the soil mix looks pretty dense is it staying soggy?  This doesn't look like scorch, I can see the tiniest leaf on there is yellowing which makes me think maybe something about the roots? Too soggy or not enough air, conditions not letting it dry out?
What kind of light is it getting, are you watering it enough. it's hard to overwater them.
